harness: Codex desktop tools; Python 3.13 isolated scripts; Poppler; Tesseract
approach: Read the frozen protocol, screened supplied page text, extracted identity and context fields, and reconciled repeated publications without loading the local corpus.
challenges: Some held files are journal contents rather than articles.
The held inventory is a separate publication from Nath.
An older PDF text utility produced control characters that confused page splitting.
The coordinator stopped the run because system disk space was low.
Line-based filtering missed restricted fragments in wrapped entries and a mixed table.
fixes: Used Poppler with explicit encoding and verified source page counts.
Separated unread intended works from the held files.
Removed 107 retained temporary images and changed OCR handling to delete each render.
Retained unresolved identities as possible duplicates.
Marked the reader exposed in every reviewed-source exposure entry.
outcome: The tables retain uncertain script status, unnumbered groups and inaccessible source leads. Illustration media stay unknown unless a primary caption explicitly identifies them. No download, package installation, corpus match or repository operation was performed.
deviations: Restricted fragments reached some tool previews; the run cannot establish reader blindness. No derived description or transcription is retained in the deliverables.
The requested raw page-text extraction preserves original source text locally; it is excluded from the tracked-file content scan.
The Sanauli held file has no entry in either supplied source register. Its text was extracted and logged, but no object row cites it.
